brief: Tidy gable-front stock barn about 32 ft wide and 56 ft long, sided in pale painted board-and-batten, set into a slight slope so a few basement stall windows show low on the downhill side. The gable end carries the farm's name hand-painted in big dark shaded letters with a scroll flourish between the lines, under a strip of small transom lights; a plain door flanked by two six-over-six windows below. Standing-seam metal roof, six-pane stall windows in white casings along the side; it sits right at the roadside with weeds along the foundation and evergreens behind.
